name: ntfy
description: Simple HTTP-based pub-sub notification service. Send push notifications to your phone or desktop via scripts.
summary: ntfy v2.24.0 (released 2026-06-04, https://github.com/binwiederhier/ntfy/releases/tag/v2.24.0) introduces an opt-in in-memory ACL cache (`auth-access-cache`) to reduce database load on high-volume servers, and fixes a critical case-insensitive ACL topic matching security bug on SQLite backends. Recent releases (v2.20.0–v2.23.0) added S3-compatible object storage for attachments, per-visitor topic creation rate limits, verified email recipient support (`smtp-sender-verify`), and several security fixes including an SSRF patch (GHSA-w9hq-5jg7-q4j7) and a SVG-based script execution fix (GHSA-j8hr-p342-xrmh). The project is actively maintained with frequent releases addressing both features and security issues.

answers.What is the current license?: Apache 2.0 (server) and GPL-2.0 (client) — dual-licensed; check repository for specifics
answers.Is the project actively maintained?: Yes — multiple releases in 2026 with active bug fixes and new features
answers.Does it support authentication and acces: Yes — ACL-based access control with SQLite/PostgreSQL backend and an optional in-memory ACL cache added in v2.24.0

breaking_excerpts: v2.20.0: ntfy will take full control over the attachment directory or S3 bucket — files matching the message ID format with no database entries will be deleted. Do not reuse the attachment-cache-dir for other purposes.
v2.24.0: Fix case-insensitive ACL topic matching on SQLite — an access control rule for 'secret' no longer also matches 'SECRET'; behavior change for existing SQLite-based ACL rules.
v2.21.0: smtp-sender-verify flag introduced requiring email address verification before sending email notifications; ntfy.sh now enforces this after AWS SES account suspension.

alternatives.name: Pushover
alternatives.review: Paid SaaS, simple API, iOS/Android apps.

alternatives.name: Gotify
alternatives.review: Self-hosted only, real-time push via WebSocket.

alternatives.name: Apprise
alternatives.review: Apprise is a powerful open-source notification library supporting 80+ services but is a library/CLI tool rather than a standalone pub-sub server like ntfy.

alternatives.name: Pushbullet
alternatives.review: Pushbullet provides cross-device push notifications with file sharing extras but is a closed-source cloud service with a restrictive free tier and no self-hosting unlike ntfy.

alternatives.name: Home Assistant Notify
alternatives.review: Home Assistant Notify supports many notification channels and is self-hosted, but requires the full Home Assistant ecosystem making it far heavier than the lightweight ntfy.
